As it becomes apparent from Figure 3, one of the obvious venues towards proving Theorem 14 is to upper bound one of SCO, or VCextr , or LR by a function of VC; note that the sign-rank cannot be bounded in such way, as was shown in Alon et al. While there are no clear ways of doing this, it can be a viable prospect of attack on these conjectures, and might be of independent interest (for example, bounding VCextr by a function of VC is Open Problem 1 in Chase et al. (2024a)). We also would like to point at a recent manuscript of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak (2025), which seems relevant from the perspective of upper-bounding LR.
context: We find it intriguing that the only known to us upper-bound of the form VC · VC∗ is from the famous construction of sample compression schemes (Moran and Yehudayoff, 2016); just as in Conjecture 16, this bound is up to log-factors.
